market_holds: HDL is a thin ADS (1 ADS = 10 HK shares of 9658, consistent with a mean -1.0% / sd 1.9% gap to HK parity over 66 traded days since May, own arithmetic from Yahoo bars). It last traded 2026-11-23 at $9.81 and had not traded on 11-24 by 14:25 ET (Yahoo chart meta). It traded on only 40 of the last 81 sessions. HK 9658 closed 11-24 at HK$7.96 (+1.4%). At USD/HKD 7.8412 that is a parity of $10.15, so the stale $9.81 sits 3.4% below parity. HK 9658 is -29.3% since the Q2 print (2026-08-26) and -2.8% over 20 days, near its 52-week low. Over the same span Haidilao 6862.HK is -21.4%, the HSI -12.7%, and HK restaurant peers 1458/9922 -25% and -32%. So most of the slide is the HK China-consumer and restaurant tape, not company news. No option chain. No dated consensus found; the newest broker targets I could see are spring 2026 Buys at HK$13.6-14.5, far above the price. No guidance. The release lands after the HK close (Q2 was filed 11:00 UTC = 07:00 ET), so HK cannot react until 11-26. Inside the window only HDL's sporadic US trades can price it. Past HDL release-day closes: Q1-26 (05-20) +3.0%, Q2-26 (08-26) +1.3%, Q3-25 (2025-11-26) -2.1%. HK's next-day reactions: +2.3%, -6.9%, +0.1%. Chinese press repeatedly reports 'post-results falls' (绩后倒跌) on earlier prints.
view: The line this stock trades on is the operating line: same-store sales and table turnover (North America especially) and operating margin. Headline net profit is driven by non-cash FX. Q1-26 had SSS +4.0% and operating margin 6.2% (+2.1pp). Q2-26 had SSS about -0.8% (NA -8.5%), operating income +119% to a 3.7% margin, and an FX-driven net loss; HK fell 6.9% the next day. Q3 is seasonally the stronger quarter, on a Q3-25 base of a 5.9% operating margin, and the margin trend has run about +2pp YoY for two quarters. Q3-26 should also carry an FX gain rather than a loss: from Jun 30 to Sep 30 2026 local currencies firmed against the USD (KRW +12%, JPY +3%, SGD +1.3%, VND +1.1%). The company's own wording ties its FX losses to local-currency depreciation. So headline net profit is likely to jump from Q3-25's $3.6M. Macro checks are flat: Singapore restaurant sales +2.6% YoY in September after a weak August. Nothing public shows Q3 same-store traffic, and NA is the weak segment. Against that, the HK slide is mostly sector and tape, so the bar is low but not obviously mispriced on this company's own evidence. The dominant feature of this window is mechanical, not informational. Entry is likely the stale $9.81, 3.4% below HK parity, and HDL usually trades about 1% below parity. Any trade between the release and 13:00 ET therefore tends to print higher by about 2%, which sits inside the 2.85% deadband. A clear operating miss (SSS negative again, NA worse) would override that, and so would a further slide in HK's 11-25 pre-release session. I lean slightly up, but not enough to act on.
unpriced: Only two small things, neither an information edge worth acting on. (1) The ADS's last print ($9.81) is about 2.4% below where it usually sits against HK parity, a microstructure gap that a release-day trade tends to close. (2) The likely Q3 FX swing to a gain will make headline net profit leap YoY, which a headline-driven US reader may not have adjusted for. Neither shows the operating line will beat.

recommendation.reason: The lean up rests mainly on the ADS's stale discount to HK parity and a probable FX-gain headline. The gap is microstructure, mostly inside the deadband, and depends on the ADS trading before 13:00 ET. The line that decides the reaction, Q3 same-store sales and table turnover, has no public leading data, and HK investors have repeatedly sold this name after prints. Below the 65 threshold, with no informational mechanism, so no trade.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Q3 same-store sales negative again, with North America turnover still falling and the operating margin not above Q3-25's 5.9%, would push it down despite the FX-gain headline.

self_critique: The up-lean is mostly microstructure. If HDL trades later today near parity, the gap is gone. If it does not trade before 13:00 ET tomorrow, the scored move is zero. The gap itself is smaller than the deadband. On fundamentals, HK investors have sold several of this name's prints, Q2's same-store sales already turned negative with NA worsening, and the 29% slide could partly reflect informed caution. A second negative SSS quarter would beat any FX-gain headline. HK's 11-25 pre-release session sits in the window and the HK tape has been weak (HSI -4.8% over 5 days).
approach_notes: P6's run-in decomposition helped: it showed the slide was sector-driven. P3's 'rebuild the line' prompted the FX-gain arithmetic. The playbook has nothing on cross-listed ADSs whose home market cannot react inside the window, or on a stale-print entry. The window's microstructure mattered more than the evidence here.
